newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MOL, MVM, MATAV HUNGARY'S TOP THREE FIRMS IN '95.
newsitem.headline: MOL, MVM, MATAV HUNGARY'S TOP THREE FIRMS IN '95.

text.p: Oil and gas company MOL , power company Magyar Villamos Muvek Rt (MVM) and telecommunications company Matav Rt remained Hungary's top three companies in 1995, according to latest rankings.

The three firms top a 200-strong list published by the Hungrian business weekly Figyelo which ranks companies according to net sales revenues. The list excludes banks, insurance companies and securities firms.
Behind MOL, MVM and Matav, which had net sales of 342 billion, 124 billion and 117 billion forints respectively, came GM-owned car manufacturer Opel's Hungarian subsidiary.

"The most significant change at the top of the list was that Opel upped its ranking to fourth place," Figyelo editor Miklos Merenyi told reporters. The firm also heads the list of top exporting companies.

The highest-ranking newcomer is gas importer company Panrusgaz, a joint venture of MOL and Russia's Gazprom, formed in 1994, which entered the list at number nine with net sales of 51 billion forints.
The second best newcomer was German Audi 's engine and turbine manufacturer Audi Hungaria Motor Kft, with net sales of 27.86 billion forints.
Merenyi said that the number of new firms featuring among the elite has fallen, with this year's top 200 featuring only seven fresh entries, compared to 40 in 1992.
The biggest climbers were the two Budapest-based Metro wholesale units, jumping to 76th and 77th place from 173rd and 178th.
Merenyi also said that Hungary's top 200 companies employed 23 percent of the workforce but accounted for 38 percent of the country's gross domestic product and 45 percent of its exports.
